chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Al-ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

The contracted slave, when he pays off something, is emancipated by the measure of what he pays off, except if his master had stipulated that if he was frustrated (from paying it) so he would be returned (into slavery). So for them is their stipulated conditions.
ai.seo_question: How is a contracted slave emancipated under Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the principle of proportional manumission (tadil) within the mukatab contract, reflecting the Shia juristic view that emancipation is a gradual right rather than an all-or-nothing outcome. It highlights the contractual flexibility where masters may stipulate a 'reversion clause' (ruju'), allowing the slave to return to full servitude if they default, a nuance that balances the master's financial security with the slave's path to freedom. This ruling underscores the ethical imperative of gradual liberation while acknowledging the legal validity of conditional agreements in classical Islamic jurisprudence.
